Not every procurement AI tool fits every pursuit team the same way. For teams whose compliance matrix work starts in Excel and whose drafting happens in Word, a tool with only a Word add-in leaves gaps in Excel and PowerPoint that pile up fast under deadline pressure. If you're weighing Procurement Sciences against other options, the differences below come down to where each tool fits in your actual workflow.


**TLDR:**


- Awarded AI (Procurement Sciences) includes a Word add-in but no Excel or PowerPoint add-ins, a gap that compounds during compliance matrix builds and late-cycle amendments
- The key split across all 7 tools is workflow scope: most cover specific phases, while few connect opportunity identification through final submission
- FedRAMP statuses vary across the field, from full Authorization to self-attested equivalency; verify each vendor's current listing before any CUI environment decision
- Teams whose compliance matrix workflow starts in Excel will find purpose-built Section L/M parsing meaningfully different from a post-draft cross-check function
- GovEagle covers the full pursuit lifecycle with Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins, an Excel-native compliance matrix, and full FedRAMP Authorization listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace


## What Is Procurement Sciences and How Does It Work?


Procurement Sciences is a government contracting AI company whose flagship proposal product, Awarded AI, spans the find, win, and deliver lifecycle. It targets a broad market, covering federal, state, local, and grants, giving it wider addressable scope than tools built exclusively for FAR-governed federal work.


Awarded AI includes a built-in CRM and pipeline module, positioning it as an integrated BD-to-proposal tool and not a standalone drafting solution. Opportunity tracking, capture notes, and proposal development sit within the same web interface, which reduces the number of separate tools a team needs to manage across a pursuit.


On the security side, Procurement Sciences holds FedRAMP Moderate Authorization and SOC 2 Type 2 certification. One structural constraint worth noting: Awarded AI includes a Microsoft Word add-in, per publicly available materials, but has no Excel or PowerPoint add-in, so teams whose compliance matrix and slide work live in Office will need to context-switch between the browser and those documents during proposal development. Procurement Sciences also acquired HigherGov in May 2026, adding a market intelligence product to its portfolio; teams evaluating Awarded AI should ask which data and workflows live inside the core product versus a separate HigherGov subscription.


## Why Consider Procurement Sciences Alternatives?


Teams running complex FAR Part 15 pursuits tend to find Awarded AI's multi-market positioning a reasonable fit when their pipeline spans federal, state, local, and grants. The built-in CRM, FedRAMP Moderate Authorization, and integrated BD-to-proposal workflow cover substantial ground in one interface.


The friction shows up in three areas for federal-focused teams.


- Office add-in gaps: Awarded AI includes a Word add-in, but no Excel or PowerPoint add-in. Compliance matrix work and pricing workbooks still happen in Excel, and orals prep and capture briefings still happen in PowerPoint, so those tasks require context-switching between the browser and desktop. Teams comfortable with that split manage it well, but proposal leads whose workflows are rooted across the full Office suite will spend more time copying between environments than the process warrants.
- Compliance matrix generation: Awarded AI's compliance function is framed as a cross-check against contract requirements, not a purpose-built Section L/M parsing workflow. For teams that generate Excel-native compliance matrices as the first step in proposal development, that distinction matters. A cross-check assumes a matrix already exists; a purpose-built workflow generates one directly from the RFP.[Chevo](https://www.goveagle.com/case-study/40-faster-proposal-prep-for-federal-contractors) , a federal contractor, cut proposal prep time by 40% after shifting to a purpose-built compliance matrix workflow, the kind of upstream change a cross-check function alone cannot provide.
- Market depth: Covering federal, state, local, and grants simultaneously is an asset for diversified firms. For teams whose entire pipeline is FAR-governed federal work with structured Section L instructions and Section M evaluation criteria, a broader tool may trade federal-specific depth for wider coverage.


## Best Procurement Sciences Alternatives


GovEagle covers the full pursuit lifecycle from opportunity search through color team review. It holds[full FedRAMP Authorization](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/goveagle-achieves-fedramp-authorization) , listed on the[FedRAMP Marketplace](https://www.fedramp.gov/marketplace/products/FR2401839361/) , distinct from equivalency claims. Teams can go from RFP to a pink-team draft with the compliance matrix generated natively in Excel and the annotated outline produced in Word. Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins let proposal teams work inside Office without context-switching. Salesforce and HubSpot integrations carry capture intelligence directly into the proposal workspace. GovEagle enforces zero data retention, and its Shipley-embedded workflow supports bid/no-bid, black hat analysis, and amendment tracking in one connected environment.


### 2. VisibleThread


VisibleThread combines rules-based document analysis with generative AI for GovCon RFP and contract review. Its workflow is analysis-first: it delivers the most value after a draft exists, which means teams still need to build the initial structure manually. No confirmed Excel or PowerPoint add-in. As of July 2026, VisibleThread holds Legacy FedRAMP Ready status on the FedRAMP Marketplace but has not yet achieved full FedRAMP Moderate authorization. A reasonable fit for enterprise teams focused on post-draft compliance review and contract analysis.


### 3. AskSage


AskSage is a FedRAMP High Authorized secure AI environment built for general government workflows, per AskSage's public disclosures. It has no Microsoft Office add-ins and no purpose-built proposal modules, meaning no compliance matrix shredding, proposal generation, amendment tracking, or bid/no-bid workflows. Teams needing a secure chat environment for general government tasks will find it capable; teams running structured FAR-governed proposal processes will find it a limited fit for that workflow.


### 4. GovSignals


[GovSignals](https://stargazy.io/proposal-tech/govsignals) covers GovCon market intelligence and proposal drafting. Compliance matrices are built within its proprietary interface, which may create friction for teams that rely on their own Excel templates. SharePoint integration is not confirmed. Per GovSignals' public security disclosures, it holds FedRAMP High Authorization and DoW IL5. Good for teams focused on opportunity research alongside basic proposal support.


### 5. pWin.ai


pWin.ai offers Shipley methodology alignment in a web-based interface. It includes a Word add-in but no Excel or PowerPoint add-ins. No built-in capture workflows or confirmed CRM integrations. Teams comfortable with web-based Shipley workflows may find it useful; teams that need Office-native drafting and compliance matrix generation across the full pursuit will encounter gaps.


### 6. Unanet


Unanet is a GovCon ERP and CRM with bundled proposal management features. Proposal functionality is part of a broader ERP offering, not a purpose-built proposal automation product. No deep Microsoft Office suite integration and no SharePoint integration. Per Unanet's public disclosures, it holds FedRAMP Moderate Equivalency, independently assessed by ControlCase (its 3PAO), with ProposalAI and GrowthStudio now available within the FedRAMP boundary. Best suited for GovCons already running Unanet's ERP who want pipeline-to-proposal continuity within one system and do not need a[dedicated proposal automation tool](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/goveagle-vs-rohirrim-proposal-tool-comparison) .


### 7. GovDash


GovDash targets government contracting teams earlier in their company maturity with AI-assisted proposal drafting and compliance support. GovDash builds compliance matrices in its web interface; teams with highly customized Excel templates should test export compatibility before committing. Per GovDash's public disclosures, it holds FedRAMP Moderate Equivalency and earned FedRAMP Ready status in May 2026, with its Federal environment now listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace following a third-party 3PAO assessment. Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins are available. A workable option for firms building out their FAR-governed pursuit workflows who want a Marketplace-listed vendor but do not yet require full FedRAMP Authorization.

## FAQ


### Why do federal proposal teams look for Procurement Sciences alternatives?


The most common friction point is Awarded AI's Office add-in gap: it includes a Word add-in but no Excel or PowerPoint add-ins, so teams whose compliance matrix work happens in Excel and whose briefings happen in PowerPoint spend time copying between the browser and those documents instead of writing. Federal-focused teams may also find that Awarded AI's multi-market scope, covering federal, state, local, and grants, trades federal-specific depth for wider coverage, particularly when pursuits are structured around Section L instructions and Section M evaluation criteria.


### What should you look for in a Procurement Sciences replacement tool?


Key criteria to assess: whether the tool generates an Excel-native compliance matrix directly from the RFP instead of running a cross-check after one already exists, whether it covers Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins rather than Word alone, and whether it holds a verified FedRAMP authorization for environments handling CUI. For teams with active BD pipelines, CRM integration that carries capture intelligence into the proposal workspace without requiring manual re-entry is worth assessing alongside drafting and compliance features.


### When does switching from Awarded AI to GovEagle make sense?


The clearest signal is when compliance matrix work creates a recurring bottleneck: if your team is rebuilding the matrix manually in Excel after drafting begins, or managing two parallel documents across browser and desktop as amendments drop, the process is creating compounding risk. GovEagle generates the compliance matrix natively in Excel from Section L and Section M before drafting starts, and amendment tracking updates that matrix automatically when the agency issues changes.


### How does GovEagle's FedRAMP Authorization differ from Awarded AI's Moderate Authorization?


GovEagle holds full FedRAMP Authorization listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace, meaning agencies can verify its security posture directly without independent confirmation. Awarded AI holds FedRAMP Moderate Authorization. For contractors handling CUI in environments where verified marketplace authorization is a contract or agency requirement, the distinction affects which tools can be used without additional security review.


### Can GovEagle replace both the proposal drafting and capture workflow that Awarded AI's built-in CRM covers?


GovEagle covers the full pursuit lifecycle from opportunity search and bid/no-bid analysis through compliance matrix generation, drafting, and color team review. It integrates with Salesforce and HubSpot to carry capture intelligence directly into the proposal workspace, so teams already using either CRM retain their pipeline data without migrating to a new system. Teams that do not use an external CRM can manage capture notes and win themes within GovEagle's capture module.
